digest.en: Trump urges Putin to pull back aggression in Europe as Washington delays its troop posture review. Simultaneously, Southeast Asia’s AI data center investments are turning into stranded assets. The geopolitical and economic stakes are tightening across multiple fronts.
digest.hi: ट्रंप और नाटो महासचिव की बैठक यूक्रेन युद्ध पर रूस की सैन्य कार्रवाई रोकने की अपील के साथ लीड कर रही है। इसी बीच ईरान पर ट्रंप का नया बयान युद्ध के अंत की तारीख़ तय करने की बात करता है।

articles.title: Contrer la menace du Jnim sur les centres urbains du Sahel
articles.summary: Al-Qaeda in the Sahel has intensified attacks on urban centers. Military responses risk worsening the human toll. Negotiated solutions may offer a less damaging path forward for the region. Ces dernières années, la branche d’al-Qaeda au Sahel a multiplié les assauts contre les villes de la région. Chercher à vaincre les jihadistes par les armes ne ferait qu’alourdir un bilan humain déjà considérable.

articles.title: Questions sur un retour en force
articles.summary: Crisis Group analysts discussed the deployment of Algerian troops in Niger. They examined how this military presence affects regional security balances. The conversation highlighted shifting dynamics in the Sahel. Dans cet épisode d’Afrique 360°, Enrica Picco et Rinaldo Depagne reçoivent Ibrahim Yahaya Ibrahim, Directeur Adjoint du Projet Sahel, Ibrahim Maïga, Conseiller Spécial pour le Sahel et Michaël Ayari, Analyste Senior pour la Tunisie et l’Algérie à Crisis Group, pour parler du déploiement de troupes algériennes au Niger et des répercussions de cette présence militaire sur les équilibres sécuritaires.

articles.title: Southeast Asia’s AI data center bets turning into stranded assets
articles.summary: Southeast Asian AI data center projects face becoming stranded assets after Nvidia halted chip shipments. The suspension disrupts the region's physical infrastructure buildout. Financial commitments now risk obsolescence. The boom's underlying architecture has effectively seized up. Wall Street spent this week celebrating Jensen Huang’s reinstatement at Nvidia as a triumph of corporate resilience and White House pragmatism. Yet while traders bid up the chipmaker’s stock in New York, the physical and financial architecture of Southeast Asia’s artificial intelligence boom has seized up.

articles.title: Threat from China looms large over Taiwan’s local elections
articles.summary: Taiwanese voters elect local officials on Saturday. The results will determine the ruling Democratic Progressive Party's political standing. Chinese authorities warn of potential interference in the process. The vote shapes the party's future global relationships. Taiwanese officials raise alarm over interference by China in elections that will shape fortunes of ruling partyTaiwanese voters go to the polls on Saturday in closely watched local elections that will shape the fortunes of the ruling Democratic Progressive party (DPP) as it navigates an increasingly precarious set of relationships on the global stage. Saturday’s vote will choose mayors, council me.

articles.title: Trump Urges Putin To ‘Pull Back’ Aggression In Europe As US Delays Troop Posture Review
articles.summary: Donald Trump asked Vladimir Putin to stop military aggression in Europe. This demand aims to facilitate a Ukraine peace agreement. Washington simultaneously delayed a review of its military footprint on the continent. The diplomatic push coincides with a strategic pause. US President Donald Trump has called on Russian President Vladimir Putin to halt all military aggression in Europe to pave the way for a Ukraine peace deal, even as Washington postpones a major overhaul of its military footprint on the Continent.

articles.title: Sibling rivalry and family bonding: How one Singapore family is preparing for Hyrox Youngstars
articles.summary: Three siblings from Singapore are training for their first Hyrox Youngstars race. Their father, a veteran competitor, inspired the family's participation. Seven weeks of preparation strengthened their bond. The focus extends beyond athletic performance to family unity. Inspired by their father, who has completed around 30 Hyrox races, three siblings are preparing for their first Hyrox Youngstars race. The Zhao family tells CNA Lifestyle how seven weeks of training have brought the children closer and taught them lessons beyond sport.

articles.title: Once Notorious Prisons, Now Luxury Hotels, Russia Redevelops Real Estate -- And Its History
articles.summary: A notorious prison in central St. Petersburg is being converted into a five-star hotel complex. This project marks the latest example of Russia repurposing historic detention sites. The development erases a significant piece of the country's institutional history. A notorious prison in the heart of St. Petersburg is being developed into five-star hotel complex. It’s the latest example of Russia’s prisons being repurposed, and with it, the loss of a key piece of Russian history.

articles.title: ‘I’m no longer a UAE official’: UN hopeful Lana Nusseibeh tries to shake off Sudan record
articles.summary: Lana Nusseibeh, the US and Russia-backed UN secretary general candidate, is touring Britain to build support. She aims to distance herself from her past as a UAE diplomat. Her record includes denying Abu Dhabi's role in arming a militia accused of war crimes in Sudan. The US and Russia’s candidate for secretary general is on a charm offensive. Can she overcome London’s resistance to her bid? Lana Nusseibeh is in Britain this week, attempting to present herself as a potential future UN secretary general, and shift the focus from her past as a United Arab Emirates diplomat who denied the country’s role in arming a militia accused of war crimes and genocide in Suda.

articles.title: Why is India so afraid of Pakistan’s Netflix love story?
articles.summary: India is restricting access to a popular Pakistani romantic drama on streaming platforms. The government views the show as a cultural threat that could shift public sentiment. This move reflects a broader strategy to control information and limit cross-border media influence. In George Orwell’s “1984”, the greatest threat to an authoritarian system is not an army approaching its borders or an enemy preparing an attack.

articles.title: Former US Admiral Sees Washington's 'Adversaries Working Together'
articles.summary: Retired US Navy rear admiral Mark Montgomery described an axis of adversaries linking China, Russia, Iran, and North Korea. He argued these nations are coordinating their actions in the Ukraine and Iran conflicts. Montgomery sees their cooperation as a growing strategic challenge for Washington. Mark Montgomery, a retired US Navy rear admiral and a senior fellow at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies (FDD), spoke to RFE/RL about the conflicts in Ukraine and Iran, which he described as connected by an "axis of adversaries" comprising China, Russia, Iran, and North Korea.

articles.title: China-Indonesia coal-to-ethanol deal is neither green nor clean
articles.summary: Indonesia and China signed a $1.8 billion deal in Shenzhen to convert coal into ethanol. President Prabowo Subianto oversaw the agreement. Partners include Pertamina and Beijing Petrochemical Engineering. The project aims to produce a liquid fuel additive for petrol. Last week in Shenzhen, Indonesia and China signed a US$1.8 billion agreement to turn Indonesian coal into ethanol, a liquid that can be mixed into petrol.

articles.title: Kim’s advanced missiles could cripple South’s economy
articles.summary: South Korea exports over 300 billion dollars from just four sectors. Semiconductors, autos, shipbuilding, and steel dominate the 700 billion dollar total. This concentration creates a structural imbalance. It also exposes the economy to significant national security vulnerabilities. South Korea’s economy is heavily concentrated in a handful of strategic industries. Of approximately US$700 billion in total exports in 2025, more than US$300 billion originated from just four sectors: semiconductors, automobiles, shipbuilding and steel.

articles.title: All hostages rescued after Colombian security forces storm supermarket, police say
articles.summary: Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella confirmed all hostages were freed after police stormed a Cartagena supermarket. The daylong siege ended with one hostage-taker killed. Thirty people had been held inside the shopping centre. Operation in which one hostage-taker was killed ends daylong siege in Cartagena shopping centre, where 30 people were initially heldColombian police have stormed a supermarket in one of the country’s most popular tourist cities, ending a daylong siege in which all the hostages were freed and one hostage-taker was killed. Abelardo de la Espriella, the far-right president, travelled to the Caribbean.

articles.title: Lululemon founder stuns Canadian women’s leadership conference with sexist comments
articles.summary: Lululemon founder Chip Wilson made sexist remarks at a Canadian women’s leadership conference. He suggested men might import brides from Thailand because women wait too long to have children. The comments stunned audience members at the event. Chip Wilson said men importing brides from Thailand was due to women waiting too long to have childrenThe controversial founder of Lululemon suggested women in Canada are having too few children and this could lead some men to bring in brides from Thailand, in remarks that stunned audience members at a women’s leadership conference. Chip Wilson, who built the Vancouver yoga-wear startup into a glob.

articles.title: RFE/RL Reporter On Being Hunted By Russian Drones
articles.summary: RFE/RL correspondent Maryan Kushnir detailed how Russian drone strikes have reshaped Ukraine's front line and increased threats to Kyiv. He described surviving a direct attack and the ongoing struggle of families searching for missing relatives. The reporting highlights the persistent danger facing civilians and journalists in the conflict zone. RFE/RL war correspondent Maryan Kushnir describes how drone warfare has transformed Ukraine’s front line, the growing danger of Russian attacks on Kyiv, his own experience of surviving an attack, and the families searching for missing loved ones.

articles.title: Girl's Death Reignites Scrutiny Of Femicide In Iran
articles.summary: Sogand Sayadi, a sixteen-year-old Iranian girl, died on November 14 after allegedly fearing her father would kill her over a romantic relationship. Her father has been arrested for the murder. The case has renewed criticism of Iran's lenient legal framework regarding femicide and the protection of women from domestic violence. Sogand Sayadi, a 16-year-old girl from Iran, allegedly told friends that she feared father would kill her after learned of her romantic relationship.

articles.title: Gaza’s widows raise their families alone: ‘We do our duties twice over, but where are our rights?’
articles.summary: Widows in Gaza now manage household duties, shelter, and education from temporary tents after losing their husbands in the war. These women describe carrying double the burden while lacking legal protections. Their testimony highlights the severe economic and social challenges facing displaced families in the conflict zone. For women in Gaza who lost their husbands in the war, providing for a family no longer means just putting food on the table.

articles.title: Emergency aid chief calls for access to war-hit communities
articles.summary: UN aid chief Tom Fletcher arrived in Yemen to warn that the war blocks access to food and medicine. He highlighted the crisis in Taiz City. Fletcher urged for immediate access to war-hit communities to prevent further suffering. The UN’s top aid official, Tom Fletcher, arrived in Yemen on Wednesday warning that the war there is preventing families from accessing the food and medicine they need to survive, particularly those in Taiz City.

articles.title: Kilmar Ábrego García, man at center of Trump deportation battle, leaves US
articles.summary: Kilmar Ábrego García left the United States voluntarily for Spain. His lawyers confirmed the departure on Tuesday. Homeland Security verified the travel. A source said Madrid was his first stop, not his final destination. Salvadorian man, who was deported in March 2025 and returned to US after supreme court ruling, leaving of own volition for SpainKilmar Ábrego García has left the United States of his own volition, his lawyers confirmed on Tuesday, with the Department of Homeland Security confirming that he was travelling to Spain. A source close to Ábrego said Madrid was his first stop but that it would not be his.

articles.title: Taliban Pressures Afghan Men To Enforce Restrictions On Their Wives And Daughters
articles.summary: Taliban authorities pressure Afghan men to restrict their female family members. Men are told to forbid women from leaving home or withhold cell phones. These measures enforce strict gender segregation. The regime uses male relatives as enforcers. Afghan men and women have told RFE/RL's Radio Azadi that Afghanistan's Taliban authorities are making men impose strict restrictions on female family members, such as forbidding them to leave the home or withholding cell phones.

articles.title: More than 300 Russians killed as Moscow props up Mali’s junta, leaked data reveals
articles.summary: Leaked records show 349 Russian military personnel died in Mali over three years. The data highlights Moscow’s support for the local junta. The figures also reveal broader Russian military activity across the African continent during the same period. Exclusive: Records list 349 deaths in three years in Mali and also shed light on Russia’s military activity elsewhere in AfricaWhen the attack on Kidal began before dawn on 25 April this year, the Russian fighters were caught off guard.

articles.title: UN deputy chief’s final call to end violence against women
articles.summary: Amina Mohammed warned another woman would be killed before she finished speaking. She called for justice for survivors and consequences for perpetrators. The UN deputy chief made this final plea to end violence against women and girls. UN deputy chief’s final call to end violence against women.

articles.title: Can conflict resolution keep pace as AI and drones reshape war?
articles.summary: The Security Council is weighing how AI and drones reshape warfare. Guterres noted these technologies are fuelling record conflict levels. Disinformation spreads rapidly, complicating peace efforts. The UN is assessing how to keep pace with these changes. When the UN was founded in 1945, computers, the internet and satellites were the stuff of science fiction. Today, artificial intelligence (AI) is already assisting in targeting, drones are reshaping warfare and disinformation is spreading in unprecedented ways, fuelling record levels of conflict.

articles.title: Concern for trapped Ebola workers as violence against women and girls deepens
articles.summary: WHO staff and Ebola responders remain trapped in a DRC hospital. Heavy fighting continues in Ituri province. The UN agency confirmed the situation on Tuesday. Personnel are stranded as violence prevents their safe evacuation from the facility. Staff from the World Health Organization (WHO) and Ebola responders remain trapped in a hospital in Ituri province, Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), as heavy fighting continues in the vicinity, the UN agency said in an update on Tuesday.

articles.title: Guterres urges renewed commitment to landmark peace deal
articles.summary: Guterres praised Colombia for progress since the Final Peace Agreement. The accord ended over fifty years of insurgency. He stressed the need for full implementation of its provisions. The UN chief urged renewed commitment to the landmark deal. UN Secretary-General António Guterres has commended Colombia for progress achieved in the decade since a landmark accord known as the Final Peace Agreement ended more than 50 years of insurgency but stressed the need to fully implement its provisions.

articles.summary: डोनाल्ड ट्रंप ने दावा किया कि अमेरिका ईरान युद्ध में जीत के बहुत करीब है। उन्होंने तेहरान को समझौते का मौका दिया, लेकिन युद्ध समाप्ति का फैसला अमेरिका करेगा। Donald Trump on Iran War: अमेरिकी राष्ट्रपति डोनाल्ड ट्रंप ने ईरान के साथ चल रही जंग को लेकर दावा किया है कि अमेरिका जीत के बहुत करीब है। उन्होंने कहा कि वाशिंगटन अभी भी तेहरान को एक ऐसे समझौते तक पहुंचने का मौका दे रहा है जिससे जान-माल के और अधिक नुकसान को रोका जा सके।

articles.summary: दिल्ली में विशेष गहन पुनरीक्षण के दौरान 47.65 लाख मतदाता सूची से बाहर हुए। इनमें से केवल 3.37 लाख ने नाम जोड़ने के लिए आवेदन किया। अंतिम मतदाता सूची 22 दिसंबर को जारी होगी। दिल्ली में विशेष गहन पुनरीक्षण (एसआईआर) में मतदाता सूची से बाहर हुए 47.65 लाख मतदाताओं में से केवल 3,37,970 लोगों ने 31 अगस्त से 25 नवंबर के बीच मतदाता सूची में अपना नाम जुड़वाने के लिए फॉर्म-6 भरा है।
